key_insight: Bayesian inference on photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion simulations can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade, separating interface-driven failure from bulk degradation.
engineering_relevance: This enables targeted stability engineering by identifying whether the hole transport layer, electron transport layer, or perovskite bulk is the dominant degradation site.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion modeling linked to experimental data
Bayesian inference to generate spatially resolved parameter maps during aging
evidence_signal: Under accelerated aging (70 °C, full-spectrum sunlight), the inferred parameter maps showed strong spatial heterogeneity and revealed the largest degradation in perovskite/transport-layer interface regions, while amino-silane passivation suppressed this effect.
watch_item: The approach depends on model assumptions in drift-diffusion and Bayesian inversion, so inferred degradation locations should be validated against independent physical diagnostics.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
